question: Which hymn from the Rigveda was used by the Brahmanas of ancient India to justify the Varna system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Purusha Sukta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Purusha Sukta**, found in the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda, is a hymn that describes the cosmic being (Purusha) as the source of all creation.
 
• This hymn is significant as it outlines the **origin of the Varna system** in ancient India, associating each Varna with a body part of Purusha.
 
• According to the hymn, the **Brahmins** (priests) emerged from Purusha's mouth, the **Kshatriyas** (warriors) from his arms, the **Vaishyas** (traders) from his thighs, and the **Shudras** (laborers) from his feet.
 
• The Purusha Sukta was later interpreted by the Brahmanas to justify the **hierarchical Varna system** as a divine and immutable social structure.
 
• It is one of the earliest references to the concept of societal division based on occupational roles and duties in ancient Indian texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Varna System**

 
 
• The Varna system classified society into four groups: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, based on their roles in society.
 
• This division was initially flexible and based on one's profession and abilities, but over time, it became hereditary and rigid.
 
• The system formed the basis of India's caste hierarchy, which influenced social, economic, and political life for centuries.
 
 
 
• **Purusha**
 
 
• The term "Purusha" in the Rigveda refers to the cosmic being or universal spirit that encompasses and transcends all of creation.
 
• The sacrifice of Purusha in the Purusha Sukta symbolizes the creation of the universe and the establishment of order in society.
 
 
 
• **Rigveda**
 
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and is composed of over 1,000 hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• It is a foundational text of Hinduism and provides insights into the early Vedic civilization.
 
 
 
• **Brahmanas**
 
 
• The Brahmanas are a collection of prose texts attached to the Vedas, providing explanations of rituals and hymns.
 
• They played a crucial role in the interpretation and justification of social and religious practices, including the Varna system.
